extra.message: Registration stores request.form["password"] directly in the User model without hashing. Database disclosure exposes every user's plaintext password.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The critical /evaluate endpoint has no authentication check. The same omission affects /lookup, /xml, and /sayhi, allowing anonymous users to invoke dangerous application functions directly.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /evaluate handler passes the attacker-controlled request.form["expression"] value directly to eval(), permitting arbitrary Python code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The /lookup handler concatenates request.form["address"] into an nslookup command passed through rp() to os.popen(). Shell metacharacters permit arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: Attacker-controlled XML is parsed with DTD validation enabled and network restrictions disabled. External entities can access local files or attacker-controlled network resources.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The /sayhi handler interpolates request.form["name"] into template source before calling render_template_string(). Jinja expressions supplied by an attacker are evaluated, enabling server-side template injection and arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: Flask debug mode is enabled while the development server listens on all interfaces. Unhandled errors expose internal diagnostics and may expose Werkzeug's interactive debugger.
